hierarchy_and_architecture_policy.heading: Organize Projects at the Right Level of the ClickUp Hierarchy
principles: Hierarchy Integrity: Workspace (Organization) → Spaces (Departments/Workflows) → Folders (Optional Project Containers) → Lists (Actionable Work) → Tasks → Subtasks.
List vs List View: A List is a container for tasks; List View is a display mode. Views present information without altering underlying structure.
Avoid Structural Bloat: Do not create a new Space for every tiny deliverable; keep Spaces lean (reflecting Free Forever 5-Space limits) and use Folders and Lists effectively.
Single-Owner Accountability: While multiple assignees can be technically configured, best practice dictates a single accountable owner per task to eliminate delivery ambiguity.

dependencies_and_scheduling_policy.heading: Know What Must Happen Before the Next Task Can Start
principles: True Dependencies: Use 'Waiting On' and 'Blocking' exclusively when hard technical, design, or approval prerequisites exist, not for vague topical associations.
Plan Awareness on Gantt: Free Forever accounts offer limited Gantt uses; scheduling must be taught in tandem with List and Calendar deadline planning.
Milestone Verification: Designate major phase completion points (Brief Approved, Creative Approved, QA Complete) as formal Milestones.
Duration vs Availability: Do not confuse calendar duration with employee work capacity; always verify team availability before setting hard deadlines.

automations_and_limits_policy.heading: Automate Small, Reliable Workflows Before Attempting Complex Systems
principles: Functioning Automation Requirement: The student must configure and successfully test ONE approved, non-destructive automation rule (e.g. status changes to 'Ready for Review' → post internal review comment).
Plan Limits Transparency: Free Forever provides up to 5 active automations and 100 actions/month; automation quotas must be verified before testing.
Loop Prevention & Error Handling: Avoid circular trigger-action loops; test baseline state, trigger event, expected outcome, and failure behavior.
Mandatory Manual Fallback: Operational workflows must have documented manual fallback checklists so project delivery never halts if quotas are exhausted.

ai_and_governance_policy.heading: Use AI for Project Assistance With Controlled Access and Human Approval
principles: Brain² & Super Agent Scoping: Covers project summaries, task drafting, and agent capabilities at an operational governance level without requiring paid licenses.
Credit Consumption Awareness: Super Agent runs consume AI Credits even when producing simple responses; administrative budgets must be monitored.
Mandatory Factual Verification: Never share AI-generated status updates without cross-referencing task completion evidence, assigned owners, and verified comments.
Synthetic Data Requirement: Real client credentials, confidential contracts, or employee salaries must never be entered into classroom prompts or practice tasks.

curriculum.title: Project Management & ClickUp Setup
curriculum.objective: Understand foundational project-management concepts and configure an organized ClickUp environment.
lessons: 1.1 What Is a Project?: Project vs ongoing operations; Defined business outcomes; Scope boundaries; Key deliverables; Timelines.
1.2 The Project Life Cycle: Initiation, Planning, Execution, Monitoring & Controlling, and Project Closure.
1.3 Project Roles & Responsibilities: Project Owner, Coordinator, Task Owner, Reviewer, Stakeholder, and Final Approver.
1.4 Project Success Criteria: Delivering agreed scope on time, within budget, and meeting stakeholder quality expectations.
1.5 Introduction to ClickUp: Workspace overview; Navigation layout; Key capabilities; Core business use cases.
1.6 The ClickUp Hierarchy: Workspace → Spaces → Folders → Subfolders → Lists → Tasks → Subtasks.
1.7 Workspace vs Space: Organization-level container vs team/departmental workflows; Designing scalable structures.
1.8 Folders as Project Containers: Organizing related work; Grouping multiple project Lists; Folder-level settings.
1.9 Designing Executable Lists: Structuring Lists for execution; Task container design; Avoiding fragmented List clutter.
1.10 Actionable Task Architecture: Writing clear, action-oriented task names; Structuring descriptions; Ownership and dates.
1.11 Subtasks & Work Decomposition: Breaking work into manageable units; Parent-child relationships; Preventing over-nesting.
1.12 Statuses & Workflow Stages: Custom statuses (To Do, In Progress, Ready for Review, Blocked, Complete); Defining 'Done'.
1.13 Workspace Roles & User Seats: Workspace Owner, Admin, Member, Limited Member, and Guest distinctions.
1.14 Sharing & Permissions Governance: Private Spaces vs shared folders; Inviting team members; Inherited permission rules.
1.15 Task Description Standards: Defining objectives, input resources, expected outputs, and acceptance criteria in task descriptions.
1.16 Project Charter & Scope Documentation: Documenting project briefs, scope limits, key assumptions, resources, and constraints.
1.17 ClickUp Docs for Operations: Authoring project briefs, meeting minutes, and SOPs directly within the ClickUp workspace.
1.18 Quality Standards for Workspace Setup: Clean navigation; Logical hierarchy; Eliminating unnecessary folder depth.
1.19 Account Plans & Feature Availability: Free Forever vs Unlimited, Business, and Enterprise tiers; Recognizing feature limits.
1.20 Setting Up a Safe Practice Workspace: Creating an isolated practice environment with synthetic data; Avoiding live client data.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Construct a simulated small-business project workspace featuring a designated Space, project Folder, structured Lists, custom workflow statuses, a project brief in ClickUp Docs, initial tasks, and an access-control plan.
curriculum.security_considerations: Enforce private space boundaries; verify guest access limitations; never use real client or employee personal data.

curriculum.title: Tasks, Dependencies & Views
curriculum.objective: Manage individual tasks, dependencies, scheduling and multiple views within ClickUp.
lessons: 2.1 Effective Task Design: Action-oriented verb-noun naming; Assigning single accountable owners; Explicit acceptance checklists.
2.2 Task Status Progression: Transitioning tasks through stages; Managing the 'Blocked' state; Establishing sign-off criteria for 'Done'.
2.3 Assignees & Accountability: Managing single vs multiple assignees; Designating primary accountability; Avoiding unassigned tasks.
2.4 Priority Levels in Business: Urgent, High, Normal, and Low priorities; Aligning priority flags with business impact.
2.5 Scheduling Start & Due Dates: Setting realistic delivery dates; Estimating task durations; Date consistency across subtasks.
2.6 Subtasks in Practice: Breaking complex deliverables into sequential subtasks; Assigning subtask owners and separate deadlines.
2.7 Checklists vs Subtasks: When to use simple completion checklists vs formal subtasks requiring separate metadata.
2.8 Custom Fields Fundamentals: Dropdown, Number, Text, Date, Checkbox, URL, and Currency property types.
2.9 Practical Operational Custom Fields: Creating fields for Deliverable Type, Department, Estimated Effort, Approval Status, and Risk Rating.
2.10 Custom Field Quality & Hygiene: Standardizing field definitions; Enforcing controlled dropdown values; Avoiding field sprawl.
2.11 Recurring Tasks: Scheduling weekly status reviews, monthly reporting, and routine audits; Configuring recurrence parameters.
2.12 Task Dependencies in Action: Understanding 'Waiting On' (prerequisites) and 'Blocking' (dependents); Impact on schedules.
2.13 Dependencies vs Relationships: Distinguishing sequential execution dependencies from general informational task relationships.
2.14 Multi-Step Dependency Chains: Mapping dependencies: Research → Strategy → Copywriting → Design → Client Review → Launch.
2.15 List View Mastery: Configuring column visibility, group-by status, sorting by due date, and inline task editing.
2.16 Board View (Kanban): Visualizing task flow across columns; Managing work-in-progress (WIP); Identifying bottlenecks.
2.17 Calendar View Scheduling: Visualizing monthly and weekly deadlines; Rescheduling via drag-and-drop; Spotting deadline clustering.
2.18 Gantt View Visualization: Visualizing task timelines, dependency connecting lines, critical milestones, and delivery delays.
2.19 Gantt View Plan Availability: Understanding plan-dependent usage limits; Navigating Free Forever Gantt restrictions.
2.20 Timeline View Awareness: Time-based resource scheduling; Comparing timeline views to Gantt charts across project types.
2.21 Practical Filtered Views: Creating saved views: 'My Tasks', 'Overdue Deliverables', 'High Priority Blockers', and 'Pending Review'.
2.22 View Personalization & Saving: Saving view settings for personal use vs saving shared views for team-wide alignment.
2.23 Views and Security Boundaries: Reinforcing that filtered views only alter visual display; Security depends on location permissions.
2.24 Dependency Schedule Testing: Shifting prerequisite dates and observing impacts on dependent tasks and final milestones.
2.25 Task Hygiene Auditing: Identifying missing assignees, expired deadlines, ambiguous statuses, and duplicate records.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Populate and structure 15+ operational tasks featuring assignees, deadlines, statuses, priorities, Custom Fields, subtasks, and at least 5 dependencies. Configure List, Board, Calendar, and Gantt views.
curriculum.security_considerations: Dependencies reflect logical task order; do not expose internal confidential reviewer notes in public view configurations.

curriculum.title: Project Planning & Coordination
curriculum.objective: Translate a project objective into realistic schedules, milestones, responsibilities and coordinated team workflows.
lessons: 3.1 Defining Project Scope: Outlining project deliverables, boundary constraints, foundational assumptions, and explicit exclusions.
3.2 Stakeholder Requirements Gathering: Analyzing client briefs; Defining operational acceptance criteria and required approval gates.
3.3 Work Breakdown Structure (WBS): Decomposing broad deliverables into work packages, executable tasks, and discrete subtasks.
3.4 Task Estimation Principles: Estimating effort hours vs calendar duration; Factoring in dependencies and review buffer periods.
3.5 Resource Planning Fundamentals: Assessing team skill sets, available working hours, competing projects, and scheduling constraints.
3.6 Capacity & Workload Awareness: Detecting task pile-ups and overlapping deadlines; Preventing team burnout and bottlenecks.
3.7 Workload Views Awareness: Understanding capacity planning features in ClickUp; Recognizing plan-tier requirements.
3.8 Designating Project Milestones: Identifying critical phase transitions: Brief Approved, Design Signed Off, QA Passed, Launch Ready.
3.9 Dependency Mapping & Risk Analysis: Mapping critical handoffs; Pinpointing single points of failure in delivery sequences.
3.10 Gantt Chart Planning in Action: Establishing baseline delivery schedules; Aligning dependencies with target launch dates.
3.11 Agile Framework Fundamentals: Iterative sprints, continuous feedback loops, backlog grooming, and adapting plans dynamically.
3.12 Kanban Principles in Project Coordination: Visualizing workflow, limiting work-in-progress, managing flow, and resolving blockages.
3.13 Scrum Awareness: Understanding sprint backlogs, daily standups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives (conceptual grounding).
3.14 Team Communication Protocols: Using @mentions in task comments, threading discussions, and posting asynchronous project updates.
3.15 ClickUp Docs for Project Documentation: Linking project briefs, scope charters, meeting minutes, and SOPs to relevant task Lists.
3.16 Meeting Coordination & Action Tracking: Structuring meeting agendas in Docs; Converting meeting decisions directly into ClickUp tasks.
3.17 Project Risk Management: Creating a basic risk register: identifying risks, assessing probability and impact, and assigning owners.
3.18 Issue Escalation & Resolution: Tracking blocked deliverables; Establishing clear escalation pathways for team roadblocks.
3.19 Change Request Governance: Managing scope creep; Assessing deadline and budget impacts of client change requests.
3.20 Quality Control & Verification Checkpoints: Establishing formal review stages; Building quality audit checklists before client release.
3.21 Stakeholder Approval Workflows: Documenting client sign-offs; Tracking revision rounds; Securing formal written acceptance.
3.22 Weekly Project Status Updates: Structuring updates: Highlights, Work in Progress, Overdue Items, Risks/Blockers, and Next Steps.
3.23 Project Closure & Retrospectives: Conducting post-project reviews; Documenting lessons learned; Archiving completed project Lists.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Draft a comprehensive project delivery framework for a chosen business scenario: WBS phases, 25 tasks, team responsibilities, milestones, dependency matrix, risk register, and quality sign-off checkpoints.
curriculum.security_considerations: Ensure risk logs contain synthetic operational data; verify that client approval records do not disclose sensitive vendor costs.

curriculum.title: Dashboards & Automation
curriculum.objective: Develop meaningful management reporting, intake workflows and one reliable, approved ClickUp automation.
lessons: 4.1 What Is a Management Dashboard?: Executive visibility; Monitoring health, progress, velocity, team workload, and delivery blockers.
4.2 Key Project Performance Indicators (KPIs): Total tasks, completed tasks, completion %, overdue tasks, blocked tasks, and milestone status.
4.3 Defining Rigorous Metrics: Formulating exact KPI definitions, numerators, denominators, reporting timeframes, and data sources.
4.4 Building ClickUp Dashboards: Creating dashboards; Adding widgets/cards; Sourcing data from specific Spaces, Folders, or Lists.
4.5 Essential Dashboard Cards: Task list cards, status pie/bar charts, calculation cards, and priority breakdowns.
4.6 Dashboard Plan Availability & Limits: Understanding Free Forever usage limits (viewing/editing limits); Operating within plan quotas.
4.7 Dashboard Data Integrity: Setting correct source locations, applying precise filters, and avoiding misleading completion percentages.
4.8 Executive Progress Reporting: Synthesizing dashboard cards into concise written reports for management and client stakeholders.
4.9 Evaluating Project Health: Combining schedule metrics, blocked dependencies, risk registers, and scope changes into health scores.
4.10 ClickUp Forms for Intake: Creating Form Views; Connecting form inputs directly to task properties in a designated intake List.
4.11 Form Availability & Plan Rules: Free-tier single-form support vs paid-tier advanced styling, conditional logic, and custom branding.
4.12 Request Intake Workflow: Client request submission → Task creation → Triage review → Priority assignment → Execution.
4.13 ClickUp Automation Architecture: Understanding the core automation syntax: WHEN (Trigger) → IF (Condition) → THEN (Action).
4.14 Practical Operational Automations: Status change updates, automatic task assignments, review notifications, and reminder comments.
4.15 The Automation ClickApp: Enabling automations in workspace settings; Admin permissions; Managing active rules across Folders/Lists.
4.16 Automation Triggers: Status changes, task created, due date arrives, priority changed, and Custom Field updated.
4.17 Automation Conditions: Adding optional filters (e.g., ONLY IF Priority is Urgent); Plan requirements for conditional logic.
4.18 Automation Actions: Posting comments, changing status, reassigning owners, moving tasks, and setting Custom Field values.
4.19 Automation Scope: Designing rules at List level vs Folder level vs Space level; Assessing impact across child tasks.
4.20 Automation Quotas & Limits: Tracking monthly action allowances (e.g., 100 actions/mo on Free); Managing active automation limits.
4.21 Operating Safely on Free Forever: Building high-impact automations within the 5 active rules and 100 actions monthly cap.
4.22 Debugging Automation Errors: Troubleshooting non-firing triggers, permission failures, quota exhaustion, and incorrect target fields.
4.23 Preventing Automation Loops: Avoiding cascading recursive triggers; Testing rules with simple, non-destructive actions.
4.24 Rigorous Automation Testing Protocol: Baseline verification → Trigger execution → Action validation → Activity log audit.
4.25 Reviewing Automation Activity Logs: Inspecting execution timestamps, action counts, success states, and error messages.
4.26 Dashboard + Automation Synergy: Ensuring automated status transitions feed real-time dashboard calculations accurately.
4.27 Documenting Operational Automations: Recording purpose, trigger event, action behavior, owner, and failure escalation SOPs.
4.28 Automation Governance: Establishing approval rules before deploying new automations; Restricting external email actions.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Assemble an executive management dashboard featuring 5 core project cards. Configure and rigorously test ONE approved automation rule (e.g. When status changes to 'Ready for Review' → add internal review checklist comment), documenting execution evidence and action quotas.
curriculum.deliverable: ClickUp Management Dashboard & Tested Automation Pack
curriculum.security_considerations: Strict requirement: verify that automation runs within active account action quotas; never configure automated external client notifications without explicit consent.

lessons: 5.1 AI in Modern Project Operations: Using AI for summarization, task generation, update drafting, and knowledge retrieval.

5.3 Brain² Plan Availability & Tiers: Understanding add-on subscription requirements, model tiering, and administrative toggles.
5.4 Model Usage Limits: Standard vs premium model allocations; Fair-use policies; Reset schedules across billing cycles.
5.5 AI-Assisted Task Drafting: Generating task descriptions, acceptance criteria checklists, and subtask breakdowns from briefs.
5.6 Drafting Project Updates with AI: Synthesizing task activity comments into executive weekly status drafts; Human editing.
5.7 AI Agent Concepts in ClickUp: Autonomous vs assisted agents; Defining operational scope, available tools, and human guardrails.
5.8 ClickUp Super Agents Overview: Agent capabilities in monitoring task progress, answering status queries, and routine assistance.
5.9 Super Agent Governance: Defining data access permissions, limiting agent actions to internal tasks, and requiring human approvals.

5.12 Cost Awareness in Super Agent Runs: Understanding that agent runs consume credits even when producing simple read responses.
5.13 Recognizing AI Hallucinations: Spotting fabricated deadlines, false completion claims, invented blockers, and incorrect owners.
5.14 Factual Verification Protocols: Cross-checking every AI statement against actual task status, verified comments, and source files.
5.15 Human Approval Checkpoints: Mandatory sign-off: project updates, deadline changes, and client communications require human approval.

learning_outcomes: Explain the foundational project management life cycle: initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.
Identify project objectives, core deliverables, boundary constraints, and stakeholder acceptance criteria.
Create and configure a scalable ClickUp workspace structure aligned with organizational operations.
Understand and navigate the ClickUp hierarchy: Workspace, Spaces, Folders, Lists, Tasks, and Subtasks.
Configure custom workflow statuses that reflect real operational stages from intake to final sign-off.
Create actionable, well-structured tasks with clear objectives, acceptance criteria, and input resources.
Decompose complex work packages into manageable subtasks while avoiding unnecessary nesting clutter.
Assign single-owner task accountability to eliminate delivery ambiguity in collaborative teams.
Set and manage business priority levels (Urgent, High, Normal, Low) aligned with project impact.
Establish start and due dates to create realistic delivery timelines across project phases.
Configure recurring tasks for routine operational reviews, weekly meetings, and compliance audits.
Configure meaningful Custom Fields (dropdowns, numbers, text, dates) to support operational reporting.
Create task dependencies ('Waiting On' and 'Blocking') to establish logical execution sequences.
Identify blocked deliverables rapidly and manage critical dependency handoffs between team members.
Utilize List views with customized column visibility, sorting, and grouping to manage daily task details.
Build interactive Kanban Board views to visualize work-in-progress, spot bottlenecks, and manage flow.
Utilize Calendar views to monitor deadline distribution and prevent milestone clustering.
Interpret and navigate Gantt charts to track project timelines, dependencies, and delivery milestones.
Build a hierarchical Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposing deliverables into executable tasks.
Identify and track critical project milestones indicating major review, approval, and launch gates.
Apply foundational Agile and Kanban principles to manage iterative project execution and task flow.
Plan realistic task sequences that account for team capacity, dependencies, and delivery buffers.
Understand team workload and capacity limitations to prevent deadline over-allocation.
Document operational decisions, meeting outcomes, and scope changes in centralized ClickUp Docs.
Communicate project progress asynchronously using threaded task comments, @mentions, and status updates.
Author structured project briefs, meeting minutes, and SOPs directly within ClickUp Docs.
Build management dashboards featuring KPI summary cards, status charts, and blocked-work widgets.
Create ClickUp Forms to capture stakeholder requests and automatically route them into task lists.
Design logical workflow automations using WHEN (Trigger) → IF (Condition) → THEN (Action) architecture.
Configure and successfully test ONE approved, non-destructive ClickUp automation with recorded evidence.
Diagnose and resolve common automation errors, non-firing triggers, and action quota limits.
Understand ClickUp automation action quotas and manage active rules within plan allowances.
Explain ClickUp Brain² capabilities across task drafting, summarization, and contextual workspace Q&A.
Understand Super Agent governance, scope limitations, human approval gates, and AI Credit costs.
Configure role-based workspace permissions across Owners, Admins, Members, and external Guests.
Protect confidential project records, financial terms, and employee data using least-privilege security.
Build an integrated project operations workspace populated with at least 25 realistic, linked tasks.
Interpret overall project health combining schedule status, blocker logs, and risk assessments.
Present structured weekly progress reports highlighting completed work, roadblocks, and next actions.
Compile a comprehensive project handover package including workspace maps, SOPs, and maintenance guides.

portfolio.title: ClickUp Project Operations Workspace
portfolio.objective: Construct and demonstrate one comprehensive ClickUp project operations workspace based on a realistic simulated scenario (Marketing Campaign, Website Launch, or Operations Improvement) featuring at least 25 tasks, 5 dependencies, Custom Fields, an executive dashboard, one tested automation, and complete handover documentation.
portfolio.countingRule: One integrated project operations workspace containing 12 cohesive components demonstrating end-to-end collaborative project delivery.

deliverables.title: Project Brief & Charter in ClickUp Docs
deliverables.scenario: Author the foundational project charter in ClickUp Docs outlining business goals, project scope boundaries, core deliverables, key assumptions, and acceptance criteria.
requirements: Documented business objective and background scenario.
Clear scope definition specifying deliverables and exclusions.
Stakeholder directory mapping project roles and responsibilities.
Documented success metrics and formal acceptance criteria.

deliverables.title: Workspace Hierarchy & List Architecture
deliverables.scenario: Design a clean, scalable ClickUp hierarchy (Space, project Folder, and dedicated Lists) establishing a logical home for all operational work packages.
requirements: Appropriate Space setup adhering to Free Forever 5-space boundaries.
Project Folder container grouping execution Lists.
Lists organized by project phase or workstream.
Standardized naming and navigation layout.

deliverables.title: Minimum 25 Realistic Project Tasks
deliverables.scenario: Populate the workspace with at least 25 actionable, non-trivial tasks across all project phases, assigning accountable owners, deadlines, custom statuses, and priorities.
requirements: Exactly 25 or more actionable tasks (not mere checklist items).
Single accountable assignee for every core task.
Clear start and due dates establishing a realistic timeline.
Priority flags (Urgent, High, Normal, Low) and custom statuses applied.

deliverables.title: Multi-Step Task Dependency Network
deliverables.scenario: Establish a verified network of at least 5 meaningful dependencies (Waiting On / Blocking) demonstrating sequential delivery handoffs and blocker identification.
requirements: Minimum 5 verified task dependencies.
At least one multi-step dependency chain (3+ connected tasks).
Clear evidence of blocked tasks waiting on prerequisite completion.
Elimination of arbitrary or circular dependencies.

deliverables.title: Custom Fields System
deliverables.scenario: Deploy practical Custom Fields that enrich task data and power management reporting without exceeding account plan allowances.
requirements: Fields for Deliverable Type (dropdown) and Workstream/Department.
Fields for Estimated Hours (number) and Approval Status (dropdown).
Field for Risk Level (dropdown: Low, Medium, High).
Standardized field definitions applied consistently across lists.

deliverables.title: Project Milestones Schedule
deliverables.scenario: Designate and track critical project completion points as formal ClickUp Milestones to anchor the delivery schedule.
requirements: At least 3 designated Milestones (e.g., Brief Approved, Build Complete, QA Passed).
Milestones linked to prerequisite dependency chains.
Clear target dates and sign-off accountability.

deliverables.title: Multi-View Workflow Suite
deliverables.scenario: Configure a comprehensive suite of project views providing different stakeholders with tailored visual perspectives on project progress.
requirements: List View with customized column visibility and due-date sorting.
Kanban Board View grouped by workflow status columns.
Calendar View showing deadline distribution across weeks.
Gantt View demonstration showing dependency lines and milestone diamonds.

deliverables.title: Executive Management Dashboard
deliverables.scenario: Construct a real-time management dashboard with essential cards displaying task KPIs, progress calculations, and blocked-work alerts.
requirements: KPI cards for Total Tasks, Completed Tasks, and Overdue Tasks.
Status breakdown chart visualizing work distribution.
Urgent/Blocked tasks alert card for immediate triage.
Accurate data source filters matching the project folder.

deliverables.title: Tested & Functioning ClickUp Automation
deliverables.scenario: Implement and rigorously test ONE approved, non-destructive automation rule, documenting successful trigger-action execution and quota consumption.
requirements: Approved rule (e.g., Status changed to 'Ready for Review' → Post review checklist comment).
Successful execution evidence verifying the action fired correctly.
Verification of active automation limits and monthly action usage.
Documented manual fallback SOP if automation pauses.

deliverables.title: Coordination & Status Report
deliverables.scenario: Draft an executive weekly status report synthesizing dashboard data into clear business progress, risk mitigations, and upcoming milestones.
requirements: Structured report: Completed Work, Work in Progress, Blockers, and Next Steps.
Risk log review with mitigation strategies and assigned owners.
Cross-referenced task IDs and verified milestone completion dates.

deliverables.title: Role & Permission Matrix
deliverables.scenario: Document an explicit permission strategy mapping access rights across Workspace Owner, Coordinator, Contributors, Reviewers, and external Guests.
requirements: Role definitions across 5 tiers: Owner, Admin, Member, Contributor, Guest.
Location-by-location permission levels (Full, Edit, Comment, View).
Guest access restrictions protecting internal documentation.
Quarterly access auditing protocol.

deliverables.title: Client & Team Handover Guide
deliverables.scenario: Author an operational handover manual in ClickUp Docs guiding stakeholders on how to navigate the workspace, update tasks, monitor dashboards, and maintain the system.
requirements: Visual Workspace Map showing Spaces, Folders, and Lists.
Task lifecycle guide explaining status definitions and 'Done' criteria.
Dashboard reading instructions and automation maintenance guide.
Documented plan limitations and update responsibilities.

assessment_model.completionRule: Students must submit the complete ClickUp Project Operations Workspace containing at least 25 tasks, 5 dependencies, an accurate dashboard, and ONE functioning tested automation with recorded evidence. A workspace with fewer than 25 tasks, broken dependencies, or an untested/hypothetical automation will not receive passing evaluation.

faq.question: What is ClickUp — Project Management & Workflow Automation?
faq.answer: A practical certification covering project planning, task organization, dependencies, dashboards and introductory workflow automation.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Five weeks with 40 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹5,900, subject to verified Nova Skills pricing and tax policies.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic task-management familiarity is recommended.

faq.question: Is coding required?
faq.answer: No. The required workflows use ClickUp's interface and supported features.

faq.question: What is ClickUp's hierarchy?
faq.answer: Workspace, Spaces, optional Folders/Subfolders, Lists, tasks and subtasks.

faq.question: What is a Work Breakdown Structure?
faq.answer: A method of dividing project deliverables into manageable work components.

faq.question: Will I learn task dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. The course teaches how tasks block or depend on other tasks.

faq.question: Will I learn Gantt charts?
faq.answer: Yes, including suitable project scheduling and plan-aware availability.

faq.question: Is Gantt available on the free plan?
faq.answer: It is currently available with usage limits; learners must check their workspace allowance.

faq.question: Will I learn Kanban?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers Board View and introductory Kanban practices.

faq.question: Will I learn Custom Fields?
faq.answer: Yes, with current plan and usage limitations.

faq.question: Will I learn recurring tasks?
faq.answer: Yes, including suitable operational use and feature considerations.

faq.question: Will I build a dashboard?
faq.answer: Yes. A management dashboard is part of the portfolio.

faq.question: Are dashboards unlimited on ClickUp Free?
faq.answer: No. Current free-plan dashboard usage is limited.

faq.question: Will I learn ClickUp Forms?
faq.answer: Yes, including basic intake workflow concepts and plan limitations.

faq.question: What is ClickUp Automation?
faq.answer: A feature that performs supported actions when defined trigger events occur.

faq.question: Does the course require a working automation?
faq.answer: Yes. The capstone includes one approved, successfully tested automation.

faq.question: Are ClickUp Automations free?
faq.answer: Basic automation capabilities are available on Free Forever within usage limits; advanced features depend on plan.

faq.question: What happens when automation limits are reached?
faq.answer: Automation actions may pause until the applicable usage reset or plan/allowance change.

faq.question: Will I learn ClickUp Brain²?
faq.answer: Yes, at an introductory applied awareness level, with optional eligible demonstrations.

faq.question: Will I learn Super Agents?
faq.answer: The course explains their capabilities, permissions, approval controls and AI-credit costs.

faq.question: Is paid AI required?
faq.answer: No. Paid AI and agent deployment are not compulsory.

faq.question: Can ClickUp manage marketing campaigns?
faq.answer: Yes. Marketing campaigns are one suitable capstone scenario.

faq.question: Can I build a website-launch project tracker?
faq.answer: Yes. Website launch coordination is another suitable scenario.

faq.question: How many tasks must I create?
faq.answer: At least twenty-five realistic project tasks.

faq.question: What must the portfolio contain?
faq.answer: Task ownership, deadlines, dependencies, Custom Fields, project views, a dashboard, working automation and handover documents.

faq.question: Is this a PMP certification?
faq.answer: No. It is a ClickUp-specific applied operations certification.

faq.question: Will I receive an official ClickUp certification?
faq.answer: The course provides a Nova Skills credential under verified institute policy; an official ClickUp-issued credential should not be claimed without evidence.

faq.question: Who should enroll?
faq.answer: Project coordinators, agency staff, team leaders, freelancers and businesses using structured collaborative workflows.
